questions.title: What should you do with your ball on each hole?
questions.question: When you start playing a hole, what do you need to do with the same ball you hit from the tee?

choices.text: Pick up your ball after a few shots
Swap your ball for another on the green
Keep hitting it until it goes in the hole
Miss your putt if it is really close

questions.explanation: You need to use the same ball from the start (tee) all the way until you hit it into the hole, unless the rules say you can switch balls.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Where you start each hole in golf.
When your ball goes into the hole.
The short grass around the hole.

questions.teachingTip: Remind juniors to try not to change their ball unless a coach or rule tells them it's OK.
likelyMisconceptions: Thinking you can change balls any time you want.
Thinking you can skip tapping in a short putt.

questions.title: What must you do with your ball on each hole?
questions.question: In general, what must a player do with the same ball they played from the tee on each hole?

choices.text: Pick it up after a few shots
Change it for a different one on the putting green
Play it into the hole (hole out)
Skip the putt if it's very short

questions.explanation: Players must play the same ball from the tee all the way into the hole, unless the rules allow them to change it.
